title: Dry Film Photoresist-based Electrochemical Microfluidic Biosensor Platform: Device Fabrication, On-chip Assay Preparation, and System Operation
protocol: Cut a PI substrate into 6-in round wafers.
Put the PI wafer in an oven at 120 °C for roughly 1 hour for dehydration baking.
Program the spin-coater to a 30-second spinning time at 3,000 rpm with an acceleration of 2,000 rpm/s.
Place the PI wafer on the spin-coater and fix it using a vacuum.
Dispense 2 mL of resist onto the PI wafer for lift-off process and start the spin-coater program.
Remove the wafer from the spin-coater and soft-bake it on a hot plate at 100 °C for 2 minutes.
Adjust the mask to pattern the electrodes on the PI wafer using UV light exposure of 400 mJ/cm² (365 nm).
Place the wafer in a bowl filled with resist-matching developer and shake slightly for 1 minute.
Rinse excess resist off the PI wafer with deionized water on a wet bench.
Dry the PI wafer using compressed air.
Deposit 200 nm of platinum onto the wafer using physical vapor deposition process.
Place the wafer in a bowl containing matching remover and remove lift-off resist while shaking slightly until all excess platinum is removed.
Rinse and dry the PI wafer as described previously.
Put the PI wafer in an oven preheated to 120 °C for 5 min to dehydrate it.
Program the first step of a spin-coater to 5 s at 500 rpm.
Program the second step of the spin-coater for 30 s at 4,000 rpm with an acceleration of 700 rpm/s.
Place the PI wafer on the spin-coater and fix it using a vacuum.
Dispense 4 mL of epoxy-based photoresist onto the wafer before starting the spin-coater program.
Soft-bake the coated wafer for 3 min at 95 °C on a hot plate.
Adjust the mask for the insulation layer on the wafer using alignment marks and an ocular lens.
Expose the wafer to 100 mJ/cm² UV light (365 nm).
Place the wafer on a preheated hot plate for 2 min at 95 °C for post-exposure bake.
Develop the resist with a suitable developer, such as 1-methoxy-2-propyl-acetat, for 2 min on an orbital shaker.
Rinse the PI wafer first with isopropanol and then rinse and dry it as described in step 1.2.3.
Hard-bake the photoresist in an oven for 3 h at 150 °C.
Place the PI wafer into the plasma chamber, fix it on the grounded plate using glass lids, and start the plasma process.
Use oxygen plasma with a standard plasma unit to remove photoresist residues.
Start the cleaning program with 200-W low frequency power, 100% O₂ flow at 250 sccm, for a total time of 3 min.
Passivate the platinum contact pads of the wafer with a UV-sensitive adhesive tape.
Cut the foil into 5 mm-wide and 11 cm-long stripes.
Attach the stripes to the wafer, protecting the parts not to be deposited with silver.
Put a sonic bath (35 kHz) into a fume cupboard.
Insert a container of silver electrolyte solution (100 g/L Ag, pH 12.5) into the bath.
Set the sonic bath to room temperature and power to 10%.
Connect the bulk contact of the reference electrodes to a constant current source.
Connect the counter electrode, a silver wire in the silver electrolyte solution, using standard cables.
Set the current source to DC with a density of -4.5 mA/cm2.
Start the sonic bath and let the current source run for 10 min.
Rinse the wafer with DI-water.
Insert a vessel of 0.1 M potassium chloride (KCl) solution into the sonic bath.
Connect the bulk contact of the wafer to a constant current source.
Connect a platinum electrode in the KCl solution to the constant current source using standard cables.
Set the current source to DC and a current density of +0.6 mA/cm2.
Start the sonic bath and let the current source run for 7.5 min.
Rinse and dry the PI wafer.
Remove the UV-sensitive tape after a UV (365 nm) exposure of 300 mJ/cm2.
Rinse and dry the PI wafer again.
Cut DFR layers to a size similar to that of the wafer (20 x 20 cm2).
Fix the desired mask onto the exposure unit.
Align the DFR layer onto the mask using the naked eye.
Illuminate the resist with 250 mJ/cm2 UV light (365 nm).
Remove the protective foil of the photoresist.
Develop the resist for roughly 2 min in a 1% sodium carbonate solution.
Shake the resist for 1 min in a 1% HCl bath on an orbital shaker.
Rinse and dry each DFR layer.
Place the PI wafer onto a transparency overhead foil.
Fix the PI wafer using standard adhesive tape.
Adjust the channel DFR layer on the PI wafer under a microscope, using alignment structures.
Preheat the top roll of the laminator to 100 °C and the bottom roll to 60 °C.
Set the pressure to 3 bar with a forward speed of 0.3 m/min.
Place the wafer with the fixed DFR layer in the middle of the laminator and start it; push the DFR through the laminator.
Repeat the lamination step after rotating the wafer by 180°.
Remove the protective layer from the front side of the DFR channel layer using standard adhesive tape.
Dispense small droplets of dissolved polytetrafluoroethylene into the wells of the insulation layer with a hand dispenser and tubes.
Laminate the cover DFR layer onto the channel layer as described in step 1.8.
Remove all protective foils on the cover and backside DFR layers.
Cut the biosensors into strips using an ordinary pair of scissors.
Cure the chips in an oven at 160 °C for 3 hours.
Adsorb avidin in the immobilization area of the channel.
Prepare a 100 µg/mL avidin solution in 10 mM PBS at pH 7.4.
Dispense 2 μL of the avidin solution onto the inlet of the biosensor.
Dispense 2 μL of DI-water on the outlet of the chip.
Incubate the chip at 25 °C for 1 h in a closed container.
Remove excess reagents through the inlet of the chip by applying a vacuum.
Wash the channel with 50 µL of wash buffer (PBS with 0.05% Tween 20).
Dry the channel for 30 s while the vacuum is being applied.
Prepare a 1% BSA solution in 10 mM PBS at pH 7.4.
Pipette 2 μL of the 1% BSA solution on the inlet and 2 μL of DI-water on the outlet of the channel.
Incubate the chip at 25 °C for 1 h in a closed container.
Remove excess reagents and dry the channel as described previously.
Prepare different concentrations (0.001-5 µM) of the DNA solution in 10 mM PBS at pH 7.4.
Dispense 2 μL of one concentration of the DNA solution on the inlet and 2 μL of DI-water on the outlet.
Incubate the chip at 25 °C for 15 min in a closed container.
Formulate a 5 µg/mL concentration of 6-FAM antibodies in 10 mM PBS at pH 7.4.
Introduce 2 μL of the antibody solution to the inlet and 2 μL of DI-water to the outlet of the channel.
Incubate labeled antibodies at 25°C for 15 min in a closed container.
Remove excess reagents as described in step 2.1.4.
Prepare a 40-mM glucose solution in 0.1 M PBS at pH 7.4 using ultra-pure water.
Preliminary treat the working electrodes with a 0.1 M PBS solution at pH 7.4 in ultra-pure water.
Electrically connect the biosensor to the potentiostat.
Ensure fluidic contact of the microfluidic channel to a syringe pump and reagent reservoir using custom-made adapter and tubes.
Start the laptop connected to the potentiostat and start the syringe pump controller.
Start the syringe pump manually using 0.1 M PBS at a flow rate of 20 µL/min.
Apply an alternating voltage of 0.8 V and -0.05 V for 5 seconds each for 30 cycles.
Oxidize the working electrode by applying a voltage of 0.8 V for 60 seconds.
Wait until the measured current signal stabilizes to start the assay readout using the stop-flow technique.
Switch the reagent from 0.1 M PBS to a 40-mM glucose solution at the syringe pump controller.
Start the software on the syringe pump controller, which will automatically stop the flow for 1, 2, or 5 minutes before restarting it.
Observe the resulting current peak.
